24:1.sourceText: τῇ δὲ μιᾷ τῶν σαββάτων ὄρθρου βαθέως ἐπὶ τὸ μνῆμα ἦλθον φέρουσαι ἃ ἡτοίμασαν ἀρώματα.
24:1.targetText: And on the first [day] of the weeks, at early dawn, they came to the tomb, carrying the spices they made ready, and certain [others] with them,

groups.note: Actual dative article and one/first numeral express the first-day time construction. English states on the first [day]; no separately printed Greek day noun or on preposition is invented.
Actual dawn plus deep qualifier is the early-dawn time idiom. English realizes that whole time expression as at early dawn without a separately printed at preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual ἃ is the accusative plural relative identifying the prepared spices. English leaves that relative link implicit, with no independently expressed which/that word; it is not the personal subject they.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR adds καί τινες σὺν αὐταῖς after the spices description. This additional group-with-them phrase is absent from pinned N1904; no extra original people or companionship words are invented.

24:2.sourceText: εὗρον δὲ τὸν λίθον ἀποκεκυλισμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου,
24:2.targetText: and they found the stone having been rolled away from the tomb,

24:3.sourceText: εἰσελθοῦσαι δὲ οὐχ εὗρον τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ.
24:3.targetText: and having gone in, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.

24:4.sourceText: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἀπορεῖσθαι αὐτὰς περὶ τούτου καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες δύο ἐπέστησαν αὐταῖς ἐν ἐσθῆτι ἀστραπτούσῃ·
24:4.targetText: And it came to pass, while they are perplexed about this, that behold, two men stood by them in clothing—flashing [with light];

groups.note: Actual ἀπορεῖσθαι is a present infinitive in the articular time construction, rendered finite are perplexed. TR has the compound διαπορεῖσθαι; the shared perplexity head is retained without replacing the actual simple ἀπορέω lemma or infinitive.
Actual καί continues the narrative after its time construction. English makes that continuation that in the it-came-to-pass frame; no printed ὅτι marker is invented.
Actual ἐσθῆτι is a singular clothing noun, whereas TR has plural garments. English collective clothing retains the actual noun head.
Actual ἀστραπτούσῃ is the flashing/lightning-like shining participle. English expands its luminous predicate as flashing [with light]; no independent Greek light noun or with preposition is claimed.

24:5.sourceText: ἐμφόβων δὲ γενομένων αὐτῶν καὶ κλινουσῶν τὰ πρόσωπα εἰς τὴν γῆν, εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτάς Τί ζητεῖτε τὸν ζῶντα μετὰ τῶν νεκρῶν;
24:5.targetText: and on their having become afraid, and having inclined the face to the earth, they said to them, “Why do you seek the living with the dead?

groups.note: Actual becoming participle belongs to the genitive circumstantial construction. English on their having become renders that circumstance without a separate Greek on preposition.
Actual πρόσωπα is plural faces. TR instead has singular πρόσωπον, followed by English face; the actual plural form remains unchanged.

24:6.sourceText: οὐκ ἔστιν ὧδε, ἀλλὰ ἠγέρθη. μνήσθητε ὡς ἐλάλησεν ὑμῖν ἔτι ὢν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ,
24:6.targetText: He is not here, but was raised; remember how He spoke to you, being yet in Galilee,

24:7.sourceText: λέγων τὸν Υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ὅτι δεῖ παραδοθῆναι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ σταυρωθῆναι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἀναστῆναι.
24:7.targetText: saying, It is necessary for the Son of Man to be delivered up into the hands of sinful men, and to be crucified, and to rise again [on] the third day.”

groups.note: Actual article/Son accusative is the subject of the delivered-up infinitive under necessity. English expresses that same subject relation as for the Son; no separate Greek for preposition is invented.
Actual article/day dative supplies the day-of-occurrence expression. English makes its temporal relation explicit as [on] the ... day without a separately printed on preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual ὅτι introduces the quoted necessity content. English goes directly from saying to the quotation without an independently written that word.

24:9.sourceText: καὶ ὑποστρέψασαι ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου ἀπήγγειλαν ταῦτα πάντα τοῖς ἕνδεκα καὶ πᾶσιν τοῖς λοιποῖς.
24:9.targetText: and having turned back from the tomb, told all these things to the Eleven, and to all the rest.

24:10.sourceText: ἦσαν δὲ ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ Μαρία καὶ Ἰωάνα καὶ Μαρία ἡ Ἰακώβου· καὶ αἱ λοιπαὶ σὺν αὐταῖς ἔλεγον πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους ταῦτα.
24:10.targetText: And it was Mary the Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary of James, and the other women with them, who told these things to the apostles,

groups.note: Actual ἦσαν is plural imperfect were with the listed women. English uses singular it was as its list-introduction frame; the actual plural form is not replaced.
Actual feminine plural article/remaining adjective is substantival for the other women in the list. English spells out women; no independently printed Greek γυνή noun is invented in this phrase.
Actual ἔλεγον is finite imperfect were telling. English uses told with an added relative who; TR explicitly has a relative/article frame before this telling predicate.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR prints an additional αἳ relative/article before the telling verb. N1904 goes directly to finite ἔλεγον without that separately printed relative word.

24:11.sourceText: καὶ ἐφάνησαν ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν ὡσεὶ λῆρος τὰ ῥήματα ταῦτα, καὶ ἠπίστουν αὐταῖς.
24:11.targetText: and their sayings appeared before them as idle talk, and they were not believing them.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

Actual ταῦτα is a these demonstrative modifying sayings. TR instead has αὐτῶν their, followed by English; the source demonstrative points to the words and is not turned into a possessive identifying their speakers.

unmappedTarget.reason: English follows TR αὐτῶν their before sayings; N1904 instead has the demonstrative these modifying sayings. No personal-possessor identity is assigned to that demonstrative.

24:12.sourceText: [[Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἀναστὰς ἔδραμεν ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον· καὶ παρακύψας βλέπει τὰ ὀθόνια μόνα· καὶ ἀπῆλθεν πρὸς αὑτὸν θαυμάζων τὸ γεγονός.]]
24:12.targetText: And Peter having risen, ran to the tomb, and having stooped down he sees the linen clothes lying alone, and he went away to his own home, wondering at that having come to pass.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

Actual πρὸς αὑτὸν is a preposition plus personal reflexive, literally to/toward himself. English expands this as a home destination. No independently printed home noun occurs in N1904 or checked TR, and the whole reflexive/home-destination interpretation is left explicit rather than equating the personal reflexive with a place noun.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR explicitly prints κείμενα as an additional lying participle before alone. N1904 has the linen clothes alone without that independent placement-state participle.

English interprets the actual toward-himself phrase as return to his own home. No Greek home noun is printed, and the whole place-destination expansion is kept unpaired rather than claiming that the actual personal reflexive itself means home.

24:13.sourceText: Καὶ ἰδοὺ δύο ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἦσαν πορευόμενοι εἰς κώμην ἀπέχουσαν σταδίους ἑξήκοντα ἀπὸ Ἱερουσαλήμ, ᾗ ὄνομα Ἐμμαοῦς,
24:13.targetText: And behold, two of them were going on during that day to a village, being sixty stadia distant from Jerusalem, the name of which [is] Emmaus,

groups.note: Actual dative relative refers to the village in the name-construction. English expresses that same naming relation as of which; no genitive source relative is substituted.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a naming copula; N1904 prints a nominal name construction without an independently written being verb here.

24:14.sourceText: καὶ αὐτοὶ ὡμίλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους περὶ πάντων τῶν συμβεβηκότων τούτων.
24:14.targetText: and they were conversing with one another about all these things that have happened.

24:15.sourceText: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὁμιλεῖν αὐτοὺς καὶ συνζητεῖν, καὶ αὐτὸς Ἰησοῦς ἐγγίσας συνεπορεύετο αὐτοῖς·
24:15.targetText: And it came to pass in their conversing and reasoning together, that Jesus Himself, having come near, was going on with them,

groups.note: Actual καί continues the narrative after the articular time construction. English uses that in its it-came-to-pass frame; no ὅτι content marker is claimed.

24:16.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν ἐκρατοῦντο τοῦ μὴ ἐπιγνῶναι αὐτόν.
24:16.targetText: and their eyes were restrained so as not to know Him,

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

24:17.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς Τίνες οἱ λόγοι οὗτοι οὓς ἀντιβάλλετε πρὸς ἀλλήλους περιπατοῦντες; καὶ ἐστάθησαν σκυθρωποί.
24:17.targetText: and He said to them, “What [are] these words that you exchange with one another, walking, and you are sad?”

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

Actual ἐστάθησαν is aorist passive third-person plural: they stood/stopped, as the narrative resumes after the question. TR instead prints second-person present ἐστέ you are, followed by LSV. The standing/stopping predicate is not relabeled as a copula or changed into a second-person source verb.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula in the nominal question What ... these words; no corresponding Greek being verb is printed there.
English follows TR second-person present ἐστέ in the sad clause, whereas pinned N1904 has third-person aorist standing/stopping. No being lemma or second-person source form is invented.

24:18.sourceText: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ εἷς ὀνόματι Κλεοπᾶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν Σὺ μόνος παροικεῖς Ἱερουσαλὴμ καὶ οὐκ ἔγνως τὰ γενόμενα ἐν αὐτῇ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις;
24:18.targetText: And one, whose name was Cleopas, answering, said to Him, “Are You alone visiting Jerusalem and have not known the things having come to pass in it in these days?”

groups.note: Actual ὀνόματι is a naming dative, literally by name. English renders the same personal naming relation as whose name; TR has an explicit relative/name frame. No relative pronoun is invented in N1904.

Actual παροικεῖς is the temporary-stranger/residing verb, attested as visiting in the primary Mounce entry. English Are ... visiting expresses that real verb, not an independent being verb or a generic sight-seeing lemma.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula in its naming clause. N1904 prints the naming dative without an independently written being verb here.

24:19.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ποῖα; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Τὰ περὶ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζαρηνοῦ, ὃς ἐγένετο ἀνὴρ προφήτης δυνατὸς ἐν ἔργῳ καὶ λόγῳ ἐναντίον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ παντὸς τοῦ λαοῦ,
24:19.targetText: And He said to them, “What things?” And they said to Him, “The things about Jesus of Nazareth, who became a man—a prophet—powerful in deed and word, before God and all the people,

groups.note: Actual article/Nazarene personal-origin designation is rendered the same person’s origin as of Nazareth. No separate Greek city-name noun or genitive place-name is invented; TR prints Ναζωραίου instead of N1904 Ναζαρηνοῦ.

24:20.sourceText: ὅπως τε παρέδωκαν αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες ἡμῶν εἰς κρίμα θανάτου καὶ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτόν.
24:20.targetText: how also the chief priests and our rulers delivered Him up to a judgment of death, and crucified Him;

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

24:21.sourceText: ἡμεῖς δὲ ἠλπίζομεν ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ μέλλων λυτροῦσθαι τὸν Ἰσραήλ· ἀλλά γε καὶ σὺν πᾶσιν τούτοις τρίτην ταύτην ἡμέραν ἄγει ἀφ’ οὗ ταῦτα ἐγένετο.
24:21.targetText: and we were hoping that it is He who is about to redeem Israel, and also with all these things, this third day is passing today since these things happened.

groups.note: Actual ἀλλά is the contrastive connector, rendered and in English’s continuation; no καί is substituted for this actual word.
Actual γε emphasis and καί addition together qualify this continuation. English condenses their joint additive/emphatic force as also; no extra English indeed or second also is invented.

Actual ἡμέραν is accusative in the time-passing construction. English makes the same day the grammatical subject of is passing; the actual accusative is retained rather than silently changed to nominative.

Actual ἄγει is present active from ἄγω. The primary Mounce entry explicitly attests its passing/spending-time use; English is passing realizes that time expression without replacing it with a different passing lemma.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR explicitly adds σήμερον in the third-day statement. Pinned N1904 has no independently printed today adverb; the actual this-day phrase is not counted a second time as a separate today word.

24:22.sourceText: ἀλλὰ καὶ γυναῖκές τινες ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐξέστησαν ἡμᾶς, γενόμεναι ὀρθριναὶ ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον,
24:22.targetText: And certain of our women also astonished us, coming early to the tomb,

groups.note: Actual γενόμεναι is the aorist becoming/being-there participle, used with the tomb destination for their arrival. English coming renders that local arrival construction without substituting an ἔρχομαι lemma.
Actual ὀρθριναὶ is a feminine plural early/morning adjective describing the arriving women. English uses early adverbially; its original adjectival analysis remains.

24:23.sourceText: καὶ μὴ εὑροῦσαι τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ ἦλθον λέγουσαι καὶ ὀπτασίαν ἀγγέλων ἑωρακέναι, οἳ λέγουσιν αὐτὸν ζῆν.
24:23.targetText: and having not found His body, they came, saying to have also seen an apparition of messengers who say He is alive,

groups.note: Actual ζῆν is a present living infinitive; English realizes that same living predicate as finite is alive in indirect speech, without changing its original infinitival form or inventing an adjective-plus-copula source.

24:24.sourceText: καὶ ἀπῆλθόν τινες τῶν σὺν ἡμῖν ἐπὶ τὸ μνημεῖον, καὶ εὗρον οὕτως καθὼς καὶ αἱ γυναῖκες εἶπον, αὐτὸν δὲ οὐκ εἶδον.
24:24.targetText: and certain of those with us went away to the tomb, and found [it] so, even as the women said, and they did not see Him.”

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object pronoun for the reported condition found at the tomb. N1904 prints found so without an independently written it pronoun.

24:25.sourceText: καὶ αὐτὸς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Ὦ ἀνόητοι καὶ βραδεῖς τῇ καρδίᾳ τοῦ πιστεύειν ἐπὶ πᾶσιν οἷς ἐλάλησαν οἱ προφῆται·
24:25.targetText: And He said to them, “O inconsiderate and slow in heart to believe on all that the prophets spoke!

groups.note: Actual ἀνόητοι is the unthinking/foolish adjective. English inconsiderate is retained in its not-considering sense, not treated as a Greek statement about interpersonal manners.

24:26.sourceText: οὐχὶ ταῦτα ἔδει παθεῖν τὸν Χριστὸν καὶ εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ;
24:26.targetText: Was it not necessary [for] the Christ to suffer these things, and to enter into His glory?”

groups.note: Actual article/Christ accusative is the subject of the suffering infinitive under necessity. English states that subject relation as [for] the Christ; no independent Greek for preposition is printed.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

24:27.sourceText: καὶ ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ Μωϋσέως καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν προφητῶν διερμήνευσεν αὐτοῖς ἐν πάσαις ταῖς γραφαῖς τὰ περὶ ἑαυτοῦ.
24:27.targetText: And having begun from Moses, and from all the Prophets, He was expounding to them in all the Writings the things about Himself.

groups.note: Actual διερμήνευσεν is aorist active indicative, whereas TR prints the imperfect διηρμήνευεν underlying English was expounding. The actual explaining/interpreting head and aorist form remain.

24:28.sourceText: Καὶ ἤγγισαν εἰς τὴν κώμην οὗ ἐπορεύοντο, καὶ αὐτὸς προσεποιήσατο πορρώτερον πορεύεσθαι.
24:28.targetText: And they came near to the village to where they were going, and He made an appearance of going on further,

groups.note: Actual προσεποιήσατο is the acting-as-if/pretending verb. English made an appearance of expresses that same represented action, not a generic visibly-appearing predicate. N1904 has an aorist form while TR has imperfect προσεποιεῖτο.

24:29.sourceText: καὶ παρεβιάσαντο αὐτὸν λέγοντες Μεῖνον μεθ’ ἡμῶν, ὅτι πρὸς ἑσπέραν ἐστὶν καὶ κέκλικεν ἤδη ἡ ἡμέρα. καὶ εἰσῆλθεν τοῦ μεῖναι σὺν αὐτοῖς.
24:29.targetText: and they constrained Him, saying, “Remain with us, for it is toward evening,” and the day declined, and He went in to remain with them.

groups.note: Actual κέκλικεν is perfect active has declined, rendered simple declined. The actual perfect form and inclining/day-declining predicate remain.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 explicitly includes ἤδη already in the declining-day statement. LSV and checked TR omit this independently printed adverb.

24:30.sourceText: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ κατακλιθῆναι αὐτὸν μετ’ αὐτῶν λαβὼν τὸν ἄρτον εὐλόγησεν καὶ κλάσας ἐπεδίδου αὐτοῖς·
24:30.targetText: And it came to pass, in His reclining with them, having taken the bread, He blessed, and having broken, He was giving to them,

groups.note: Actual κατακλιθῆναι is an aorist passive infinitive in the articular time construction, used for reclining at a meal. English reclining retains that posture predicate without inventing a present Greek participle.

24:31.sourceText: αὐτῶν δὲ διηνοίχθησαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ, καὶ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτόν· καὶ αὐτὸς ἄφαντος ἐγένετο ἀπ’ αὐτῶν.
24:31.targetText: and their eyes were opened, and they recognized Him, and He became unseen by them.

groups.note: Actual ἀπ’ αὐτῶν is a from-them separation phrase with becoming unseen. English renders the same people as the observers by whom He is unseen; the actual ἀπό remains, not a substituted ὑπό agent preposition or a claim that they caused the disappearance.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

24:32.sourceText: καὶ εἶπαν πρὸς ἀλλήλους Οὐχὶ ἡ καρδία ἡμῶν καιομένη ἦν ἐν ἡμῖν, ὡς ἐλάλει ἡμῖν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, ὡς διήνοιγεν ἡμῖν τὰς γραφάς;
24:32.targetText: And they said to one another, “Was our heart not burning within us as He was speaking to us in the way, and as He was opening the Writings up to us?”

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR explicitly prints καί before the second as/opening description. N1904 repeats ὡς without that additional coordinator; no extra Greek καί is invented.

24:33.sourceText: Καὶ ἀναστάντες αὐτῇ τῇ ὥρᾳ ὑπέστρεψαν εἰς Ἱερουσαλήμ, καὶ εὗρον ἠθροισμένους τοὺς ἕνδεκα καὶ τοὺς σὺν αὐτοῖς,
24:33.targetText: And they, having risen up the same hour, turned back to Jerusalem, and found the Eleven gathered together, and those with them,

groups.note: Actual ἠθροισμένους is a perfect nonactive gathering participle from the simple ἀθροίζω lemma. English gathered together realizes its collective gathering action; TR instead has the συν- compound. No extra N1904 compound prefix or together word is invented.

24:34.sourceText: λέγοντας ὅτι ὄντως ἠγέρθη ὁ Κύριος καὶ ὤφθη Σίμωνι.
24:34.targetText: saying, “The Lord was indeed raised, and was seen by Simon”;

unmappedSource.reason: Actual ὅτι introduces the reported statement. English marks the report with direct quotation rather than an independently written that word.

24:35.sourceText: καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐξηγοῦντο τὰ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ καὶ ὡς ἐγνώσθη αὐτοῖς ἐν τῇ κλάσει τοῦ ἄρτου.
24:35.targetText: and they were expounding the things in the way, and how He was made known to them in the breaking of the bread,

24:36.sourceText: Ταῦτα δὲ αὐτῶν λαλούντων αὐτὸς ἔστη ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν [[καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Εἰρήνη ὑμῖν]].
24:36.targetText: and as they are speaking these things, Jesus Himself stood in the midst of them, and says to them, “Peace to you”;

groups.note: Actual speaking present participle belongs to the genitive time circumstance. English realizes that same circumstance as as they are speaking; no independent Greek as or finite being verb is invented.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR repeats the Jesus name after Himself. N1904 has the same personal subject pronoun but no independently printed Jesus name here; no name lemma is assigned to the pronoun.

24:37.sourceText: πτοηθέντες δὲ καὶ ἔμφοβοι γενόμενοι ἐδόκουν πνεῦμα θεωρεῖν.
24:37.targetText: and being amazed, and becoming frightened, they were thinking themselves to see a spirit.

groups.note: Actual πτοηθέντες is an aorist passive alarm/startling participle from πτοέω. English being amazed is retained as that startled/alarmed reaction, not substituted with a θαυμάζω wondering lemma or a present Greek participle.

Actual ἐδόκουν is the thinking/supposing predicate with its own understood plural subject. English expands the indirect-sight construction as they were thinking themselves; no independently printed reflexive pronoun is invented.

24:38.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τί τεταραγμένοι ἐστέ, καὶ διὰ τί διαλογισμοὶ ἀναβαίνουσιν ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ ὑμῶν;
24:38.targetText: And He said to them, “Why are you troubled? And why do reasonings come up in your hearts?

groups.note: Actual καρδίᾳ is singular heart, whereas TR prints plural καρδίαις and English uses hearts. The real singular source noun remains unchanged.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

24:39.sourceText: ἴδετε τὰς χεῖράς μου καὶ τοὺς πόδας μου, ὅτι ἐγώ εἰμι αὐτός· ψηλαφήσατέ με καὶ ἴδετε, ὅτι πνεῦμα σάρκα καὶ ὀστέα οὐκ ἔχει καθὼς ἐμὲ θεωρεῖτε ἔχοντα.
24:39.targetText: See My hands and My feet, that I am He; handle Me and see, because a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you see Me having.”

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

24:40.sourceText: [[καὶ τοῦτο εἰπὼν ἔδειξεν αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας καὶ τοὺς πόδας.]]
24:40.targetText: And having said this, He showed the hands and the feet to them,

groups.note: Actual ἔδειξεν is the simple δείκνυμι showing verb, while TR prints the ἐπι- compound. English He showed retains the shared showing head without inventing the longer N1904 compound.

24:41.sourceText: ἔτι δὲ ἀπιστούντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς καὶ θαυμαζόντων, εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἔχετέ τι βρώσιμον ἐνθάδε;
24:41.targetText: and while they are not believing from the joy, and wondering, He said to them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”

groups.note: Actual ἀπιστούντων is a present disbelieving participle in a genitive time circumstance. English expands it as while ... are not believing; no independent Greek while/negative/finite-being words are claimed.
Actual βρώσιμον is the edible adjective modifying anything. English verbalizes that edible property as to eat; no Greek eating infinitive or agent/person form is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: Actual ἔτι marks still in this continuing-disbelief circumstance. English states the while circumstance but does not separately express still; the Greek duration adverb is not relabeled a while conjunction.

24:42.sourceText: οἱ δὲ ἐπέδωκαν αὐτῷ ἰχθύος ὀπτοῦ μέρος·
24:42.targetText: And they gave to Him part of a broiled fish, and of a honeycomb,

unmappedTarget.reason: TR explicitly adds the honeycomb phrase after the fish portion. Pinned N1904 has no corresponding added food noun or coordinating/prepositional words.

24:43.targetText: and having taken, He ate before them,

24:44.sourceText: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς Οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι μου οὓς ἐλάλησα πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἔτι ὢν σὺν ὑμῖν, ὅτι δεῖ πληρωθῆναι πάντα τὰ γεγραμμένα ἐν τῷ νόμῳ Μωϋσέως καὶ τοῖς προφήταις καὶ ψαλμοῖς περὶ ἐμοῦ.
24:44.targetText: and He said to them, “These [are] the words that I spoke to you, being yet with you, that it is necessary to be fulfilled all the things that are written in the Law of Moses, and the Prophets, and the Psalms, about Me.”

unmappedSource.reason: Actual μου is the first-person possessive of these words. English and checked TR omit this independently written My word; the later actual Me belongs to the writings-about-Me phrase and is not reused to erase the omission.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula in the initial These ... the words nominal statement; no corresponding Greek being verb is printed at that point.

24:45.sourceText: τότε διήνοιξεν αὐτῶν τὸν νοῦν τοῦ συνιέναι τὰς γραφάς· καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς
24:45.targetText: Then He opened up their understanding to understand the Writings,

sourceMoved.reason: The actual and/said/to-them reporting frame is printed at the end of raw Greek24:45 but rendered at the beginning of English24:46. Its true original identities remain24:45; these three words are exclusively moved, not duplicated.

24:47.sourceText: καὶ κηρυχθῆναι ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ μετάνοιαν εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν εἰς πάντα τὰ ἔθνη,— ἀρξάμενοι ἀπὸ Ἱερουσαλήμ.
24:47.targetText: and conversion and forgiveness of sins is to be proclaimed in His Name to all the nations, beginning from Jerusalem:

groups.note: Actual κηρυχθῆναι is an aorist passive proclaiming infinitive under the reported written content. English realizes that same predicate as finite is to be proclaimed without inventing a separate Greek being/necessity word.
Actual ἐπί with the dative name is rendered in in the English name relation. The actual ἐπί remains rather than a substituted ἐν occurrence.
Actual μετάνοιαν is the change-of-mind/repentance noun, rendered conversion. Its actual μετάνοια head remains, not an invented ἐπιστροφή noun or turning verb.

Actual ἀρξάμενοι is an aorist middle nominative masculine plural participle. TR instead has accusative singular ἀρξάμενον. English beginning is retained with the actual N1904 plural nominative form visible, not silently assigned TR’s case/number.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

Actual εἰς introduces forgiveness as the repentance-to/forgiveness relation. TR instead prints coordinating καί, followed by English and; the prepositional and coordinating heads are not treated as identical.

unmappedTarget.reason: English follows TR καί coordinating conversion and forgiveness, whereas N1904 prints εἰς introducing forgiveness. No coordinating καί is invented for that actual preposition.

24:48.targetText: and you are witnesses of these things.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a continuing and absent from N1904. Checked TR has δέ in this clause; no independent N1904 coordinator is printed.

24:49.sourceText: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ ἐξαποστέλλω τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ Πατρός μου ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς· ὑμεῖς δὲ καθίσατε ἐν τῇ πόλει ἕως οὗ ἐνδύσησθε ἐξ ὕψους δύναμιν.
24:49.targetText: And behold, I send the promise of My Father on you, but you—abide in the city of Jerusalem until you are clothed with power from on high.”

groups.note: Actual ἐξαποστέλλω is the send-out compound, while TR has simple ἀποστέλλω. English send retains the shared sending head without replacing the actual source lemma.

Actual καθίσατε is an aorist active imperative of καθίζω, whose remain/stay use is explicitly attested for Luke24:49 by the primary Mounce entry. English abide uses that lexical sense; no different μένω lemma is substituted.

Actual ἐνδύσησθε is an aorist middle subjunctive putting-on/clothing form. English uses the passive-style you are clothed; the actual middle voice and subjunctive form remain rather than being retagged passive indicative.

unmappedTarget.reason: TR adds the Jerusalem name to the city phrase. Pinned N1904 prints the city without independently repeating this name; the nearby travel destinations in other verses are not borrowed.

24:50.sourceText: Ἐξήγαγεν δὲ αὐτοὺς ἕως πρὸς Βηθανίαν, καὶ ἐπάρας τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ εὐλόγησεν αὐτούς.

groups.note: Actual Ἐξήγαγεν is the bringing/leading-out compound, expanded as He led ... forth outside. English repeats that single outward-direction feature, and TR also prints a separate ἔξω outside adverb. No extra N1904 adverb or second leading predicate is invented.

Actual ἕως πρὸς gives the extent/direction relation as far as toward the Bethany destination. English condenses it as to; TR has ἕως εἰς. Both actual words retain their original identities, not a replaced εἰς.

24:51.sourceText: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εὐλογεῖν αὐτὸν αὐτοὺς διέστη ἀπ’ αὐτῶν [[καὶ ἀνεφέρετο εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν]].

groups.note: Actual διέστη is aorist active intransitive separating/parting. English uses passive-style He was parted for that same separation event; no Greek passive form or independently stated external agent is invented.

24:52.targetText: and they, having worshiped Him, turned back to Jerusalem with great joy,
